reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had. His lectures have nothing to do with the course. He expects students to know the material beforehand; however, his slides are never uploaded before said class. Review sessions have nothing to do with exams. No extra credit. Final contained problems never reviewed before in class. Avoid if possible.

Presents the class with a clear grading criterion & emphasizes studying lecture notes, yet creates tests based on deeper understanding that isn't elaborated. Whenever asked to explain something, he will likely state that you must figure out the answer yourself. Prepare to learn separately and study as if you were a chem major; late work = zero.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Expected students to study more than 15 hours a week for his course. I understand it's a heavy science course but he was incredibly unreasonable and insensitive towards personal circumstances. Strict grader and went off of his own rubric rather than the departments. Avoid him at all costs, very egocentric and demanding.

Emphasized that he wanted his students to be prepared for grad school by exposing them to advanced material (then don't teach undergrad). Administration lets him get away with anything since there is no options to replace him. Was a very strict grader too, I refuse to every take another one of his courses. I still don't know how he's a professor.

He knows his stuff but fails to engage students in the lecture. Personally, I taught myself everything in his class and his exam reviews were misleading because in the test he'd give you the same question but one of the harder “exceptions” that isn't covered on the exam reviews.

I don't recommend this professor because when the class asked a question about the lecture, he would say “ That's something you will need to find out”. He would not help you and leave it up to you to find out.

Do not take any classes with him. I would ask stuff during his office hours because I was having a hard time understanding the lecture, and he would just read me the question repeatedly. I was taking an introduction to chemistry, and he said I should already know that. Which makes no sense, and that is why I was taking Introduction to Chemistry.

Dr. Cremar's is notoriously difficult. Even if you do bad on his exams, you'll be fine if you do good on the good on Iclicker participation, Aleks assignments, and the lab portion of the class. His test reviews help understand the material being covered on the exams.
You'll be fine if you put in the work.
